units.translation: where the use of the aorist passive ἐπαίσθην [I was struck] is to be noted. For the Attic writers usually take the passive aorist from the verb πλήσσω [to strike] as ἐπλήγην [I was struck], but they preferred the active ἔπαισα [I struck] to the aorist ἔπληξα [I struck]: hence Sophocles Ant. 171 preferred to say παίσαντές τε καὶ πληγέντες [both having struck and having been struck] rather than παισθέντες [having been struck], and likewise others, examples of which Nauck collected in Mélanges Greco-Romains vol. 2 p. 468. From this, however, it does not follow that Aeschylus was not allowed to say παισθείς [having been struck] and ἐπαίσθην [I was struck] for πληγείς [having been struck] and ἐπλήγην [I was struck].
